The '''Willie Mays World Series Most Valuable Player''' ('''MVP''') '''Award''' is given to the [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) player deemed to have the most impact on his team's performance in the [[World Series]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.startribune.com/blogs/56922227.html?elr=KArksi8cyaiUBP7hUiD3aPc:_Yyc:aUU|title=Thursday (Derek Jeter over Joe Mauer for MVP?) edition: Wha' Happened?|last=Rand|first=Michael|date=September 3, 2009|work=Minneapolis Star-Tribune|access-date=September 12, 2009|archive-date=August 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140802203542/http://www.startribune.com/blogs/56922227.html?elr=KArksi8cyaiUBP7hUiD3aPc:_Yyc:aUU|url-status=dead}}</ref> which is the final round of the [[Major League Baseball postseason|MLB postseason]]. The award was first presented in 1955 by ''[[Sport (American magazine)|Sport]]'' magazine,<ref>{{cite book|last=Dickson|first=Paul|title=The Dickson Baseball Dictionary|year=2011|publisher=W. W. Norton & Company|page=945|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ceeU7xSLw5kC&q=%22SPORT%20Magazine%20Award%22%20baseball&pg=PA945|access-date=October 31, 2019|quote=The SPORT Magazine Award, an annual award presented since 1955, originally by SPORT magazine in cooperation with the Chevrolet Motor Co. (the magazine ceased publication in 2000 and is no longer involved with the award).|isbn=9780393073492|edition=Third}}</ref> but since 1985 has been officially presented by MLB.<ref name=saberhagen/> The winner is determined during the final game of the World Series by a committee of reporters and officials present at the game.

On September 29, 2017, the award was renamed in honor of [[Willie Mays]] in remembrance of the 63rd anniversary of [[The Catch (baseball)|The Catch]], which occurred the year before the award's debut;<ref name="mayshonored">{{cite news|last=Adler|first=David|title=World Series MVP Award renamed for Mays|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/world-series-mvp-award-renamed-for-willie-mays-c256686298|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|website=[[MLB.com]]|date=September 29, 2017|access-date=September 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001054021/http://m.mlb.com/news/article/256686298/world-series-mvp-award-renamed-for-willie-mays/ |archive-date=October 1, 2017 |url-status=live|via=[[Wayback Machine]]}}</ref> Mays never won the award himself.

==Car and trophy==
[[File:Willie_Mays_1961.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Willie Mays, namesake of the award since 2017; he himself never won the honor.]]

The award winner has traditionally received a new car.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-courier-journal-gibson-wins-sports-c/158311314/ |title=Gibson Wins Sports Car As World Series' MVP |agency=[[United Press International|UPI]] |newspaper=[[Courier Journal]] |location=[[Louisville, Kentucky]] |page=B6 |date=October 13, 1967 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> [[Johnny Podres]], the inaugural winner in 1955, received a [[Chevrolet Corvette]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/herald-and-review-untitled/158342630/ |title=(untitled) |newspaper=[[Herald & Review]] |location=[[Decatur, Illinois]] |page=17 |date=October 12, 1955 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> The 1977 winner, [[Reggie Jackson]], received a [[Ford Thunderbird]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-evening-sun-yankees-should-have-won/158313394/ |title=Yankees Should Have Won Easily |first=Bill |last=Tanton |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun|The Evening Sun]] |location=Baltimore, Maryland |page=C4 |date=October 20, 1977 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> while the 1983 winner, [[Rick Dempsey]], received a [[Pontiac Firebird]].<ref name=dempsey>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/culpeper-star-exponent-rick-dempsey/158337811/ |title=Rick Dempsey |newspaper=[[Culpeper Star-Exponent]] |location=[[Culpeper, Virginia]] |page=7 |date=October 28, 1983 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> [[Frank Viola]], the 1987 MVP, received a [[Volvo 740]].<ref name=viola>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-manhattan-mercury-viola-collects-ser/158338875/ |title=Viola collects Series awards |newspaper=[[The Manhattan Mercury]] |location=[[Manhattan, Kansas]] |page=B7 |first=Thomas |last=Rogers |agency=[[New York Times News Service]] |date=November 1, 1987 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref>

Since 2004, [[General Motors]] had provided the vehicle.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://carbuzz.com/news/world-series-mvp-has-to-wait-for-his-2020-corvette |title = World Series MVP Has to Wait for His 2020 Corvette |website=carbuzz.com |date = November 1, 2019}}</ref><ref name=rivard/> Examples include [[David Ortiz]] (2013 MVP) receiving a 2014 [[Chevrolet Silverado]] High Country, [[Ben Zobrist]] (2016 MVP) receiving a 2017 [[Chevrolet Camaro]] SS Convertible 50th Anniversary Edition, and [[Corey Seager]] (2020 MVP) receiving a 2021 [[Chevrolet Tahoe]] Z71.<ref name=rivard>{{cite web |url=https://www.guideautoweb.com/en/galleries/57579/world-series-mvps-and-their-cars/ |title=World Series MVPs and Their Cars |first=Guillaume |last=Rivard |website=guideautoweb.com |date=October 28, 2020 |accessdate=November 2, 2024}}</ref>

A trophy has also been presented to the award winner since at least the late 1970s.<!--1978 is currently the earliest documented example--> In 1985, [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) took over as the official award presenter from ''[[Sport (American magazine)|Sport]]'' magazine,<ref name=saberhagen>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/journal-tribune-saberhagen-collects-worl/158340397/ |title=Saberhagen collects World Series MVP trophy |first=Lisa |last=Harris |agency=[[United Press International|UPI]] |newspaper=[[Journal Tribune]] |location=[[Biddeford, Maine]] |page=16 |date=November 5, 1985 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> although for a few years, MLB and ''Sport'' each presented different trophies to the winner.<ref name=bowl/><ref name=viola/> Trophies given to award winners include:

*A wooden base supporting a metallic baseball inside a hoop;<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-minneapolis-star-mike-schmidt-displa/158314301/ |title=Mike Schmidt displayed World Series MVP trophy |agency=[[Associated Press|AP]] |newspaper=[[The Minneapolis Star]] |page=10B |date=October 29, 1980 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref><ref name=dempsey/> in use by 1978,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/asbury-park-press-bucky-dent-hoists-the/158313964/ |title=Bucky Dent hoists the World Series MVP trophy |agency=[[Associated Press|AP]] |newspaper=[[Asbury Park Press]] |location=[[Asbury Park, New Jersey]] |page=D3 |date=October 24, 1978 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> and last presented in 1984.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/petoskey-news-review-great-day-for-alan/158338064/ |title=Great Day for Alan Trammell |first=Milton |last=Richman |agency=[[United Press International|UPI]] |newspaper=[[Petoskey News-Review]] |location=[[Petoskey, Michigan]] |page=16 |date=October 25, 1984 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref>
*A tall wooden base with a metallic baseball on top, surrounded by a number of metallic flags; first presented in 1985,<ref name=showing>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-state-showing-off-his-prize/158338450/ |title=Showing off his prize |newspaper=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]] |location=[[Columbia, South Carolina]] |page=4-B |date=November 5, 1985 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref><ref name=viola/> and last presented in 1988.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-macon-telegraph-orel-hershiser-with/158341600/ |title=Orel Hershiser with World Series MVP trophy |newspaper=[[The Telegraph (Macon, Georgia)|The Telegraph]] |location=[[Macon, Georgia]] |page=Sports 6 |date=October 29, 1988 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> The text on this trophy read "''Sport Magazine's'' World Series Most Valuable Player Award".<ref name=showing/>
*A metallic bowl on a wooden base; in use by 1987,<ref name=bowl>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/auburn-journal-frank-viola/158340826/ |title=Frank Viola |newspaper=[[Auburn Journal]] |location=[[Auburn, California]] |page=B1 |date=October 27, 1987 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref> apparently the MLB-awarded trophy.
*A trapezoidal wooden base, which included the MLB logo, topped by a metallic baseball; first awarded in 1988.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/detroit-free-press-orel-hershiser/158341201/ |title=Orel Hershiser |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |page=1C |date=October 22, 1988 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref>
* A pyramid-shaped trophy with a dark base, clear body, and baseball on top; in use by 1995.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-charlotte-observer-vindication/158342254/ |title=Vindication |newspaper=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |page=9 |date=October 30, 1995 |accessdate=November 2, 2024 |via=newspapers.com}}</ref>
*A scaled-down variant of the [[Commissioner's Trophy (MLB)|Commissioner's Trophy]] with a single large metallic pennant; last presented in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/willie-mays-world-series-mvp-george-springer-of-the-houston-news-photo/869232372 |title=2017 Major League Baseball World Series Game Seven: Houston Astros v. Los Angeles Dodgers |website=gettyimages.com |date=November 1, 2017 |accessdate=November 2, 2024}}</ref> 
*A wooden pedestal topped by a bronze sculpture of Willie Mays making "[[The Catch (baseball)|The Catch]]" in the [[1954 World Series]]; in use since 2018.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://autoinformed.com/boston-tramples-los-angeles-takes-2018-world-series-in-5/major-league-baseballs-2018-willie-mays-world-series-most-valuable-player-steve-pearce-of-the-boston-red/ |title=Major League Baseball's 2018 Willie Mays World Series Most Valuable Player Steve Pearce of the Boston Red |first=Ken |last=Zino |website=autoinformed.com |date=October 29, 2018 |accessdate=November 2, 2024}}</ref>

===Winners by team and by position===
[[File:Bobby Richardson 1963.JPG|thumb|right|150px|Bobby Richardson, the only second baseman to have won the award]]

From 1955 through 2025, a total of 71 seasons, there have been 70 editions of the World Series played (there was no World Series in {{wsy|1994}}). In 68 editions, a single MVP was named; in 1981, three MVPs were named; and in 2001, two MVPs were named. Thus, there have been a total of 73 MVPs.

The position at which players have won the most MVPs is [[pitcher]], 30 times. Four of those winners were exclusively [[relief pitcher]]s, the most recent being [[Mariano Rivera]] in 1999. Twelve of the first 14 MVPs were pitchers. From 1969 through 1986, the prevalence of pitcher MVPs declined, as only two pitchers won the award during this period. From 1987 through 1991, all of the MVPs were pitchers. Since 1995, {{years ago|1995}} years ago, pitchers have won the award eleven times, the most recent being [[Yoshinobu Yamamoto]] in 2025.

The most uncommon position for an MVP is [[second baseman]], with only [[Bobby Richardson]] in 1960 winning at the position. Richardson is also the only MVP to be named from a losing World Series team.

Of the 30 current MLB franchises, 24 have had at least one MVP. The six that have not are the [[Cleveland Guardians]], [[Colorado Rockies]], [[Milwaukee Brewers]], [[San Diego Padres]], [[Seattle Mariners]], and [[Tampa Bay Rays]]. Of those six franchises, five have never won a World Series with Seattle never having been in a World Series and Cleveland last won in 1948, prior to the MVP award being established.

==Notable accomplishments==
{{multiple image
| align = right
| perrow = 2
| direction = horizontal
| footer_align = left
| total_width = 250
| image1 = Sandy Koufax.jpg
| image2 = Bob Gibson 1962.png
| image3 = Reggie Jackson October 1973.jpeg
| image4 = Corey_Seager_on_September_5,_2015.jpg
| footer = [[Sandy Koufax]], [[Bob Gibson]], [[Reggie Jackson]], and [[Corey Seager]] are the only players who have been named World Series MVP multiple times; each won the award twice.
}}

Four players have won the award twice: [[Sandy Koufax]] (1963, 1965), [[Bob Gibson]] (1964, 1967), [[Reggie Jackson]] (1973, 1977), and [[Corey Seager]] (2020, 2023). Jackson and Seager are the only players to have won the award with two different teams, while Seager is the first player to win the award in both leagues.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Blum |first1=Ronald |title=Corey Seager earns second World Series MVP, joining Sandy Koufax, Bob Gibson and Reggie Jackson |url=https://apnews.com/article/corey-seager-world-series-mvp-fd32972a8578a820698917490431eae9 |work=[[AP News]] |date=November 2, 2023}}</ref> Additionally, Koufax, Gibson, and Jackson all won their first MVP's playing against a team that [[Yogi Berra]] either played or managed (1963 - played for the Yankees, 1964 - managed the Yankees, and 1973 - managed the Mets).

A total of 13 players born outside of the United States have been named World Series MVP, with [[Pedro Guerrero (baseball, born 1956)|Pedro Guerrero]], a native of the [[Dominican Republic]], being the first to win it in 1981. Of players born outside the U.S., the Dominican Republic has produced the most World Series MVP winners, with five. [[Venezuela]], [[Cuba]], and [[Japan]] have produced two each, and [[Colombia]], and [[Panama]] have each produced one. California-born [[Freddie Freeman]], the 2024 MVP, holds dual citizenship in both the U.S. and Canada.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Joseph |first=Andrew |date=February 8, 2017 |title=The heartfelt reason California-raised Freddie Freeman will play for Canada in the WBC |work=USA Today |url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/02/california-born-freddie-freeman-braves-wbc-canada-world-baseball-classic-mother-mlb |access-date=February 9, 2017}}</ref>

===Pitchers===
*[[Johnny Podres]] won the inaugural award in 1955, with the [[Brooklyn Dodgers]]. Podres, with a 9–10 [[Win–loss record (pitching)|win–loss record]] during the regular season, beat the Yankees twice in the series; both victories were [[complete game]]s.<ref name="ws1955"/>
*[[Don Larsen]] won the 1956 award after pitching the only individual [[no-hitter]] in World Series history, in the fifth game of the series; the no-hitter was also a [[Perfect game (baseball)|perfect game]].<ref name="nh">{{cite news|last=Robinson|first=Joshua|title=Live Analysis: Twins vs. Yankees|url=http://bats.blogs.nytimes.com/2009/10/09/analysis-from-the-ballpark-twins-vs-yankees-2/?pagemode=print|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=October 9, 2009|access-date=October 23, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mlb.mlb.com/mlb/baseballs_best/mlb_bb_gamepage.jsp?story_page=bb_56ws_gm5_bknnyy|title= 1956 World Series: Game 5; Three words: Larsen's Perfect Game|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|website=[[MLB.com]]|access-date=October 2, 2009}}</ref>
*[[Bruce Hurst]] of the [[Boston Red Sox]] had been voted MVP of the [[1986 World Series]] during Game 6,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2015/12/01/catching-with-bruce-hurst-series-mvp-who-wasn/Vp5tPmoGkE9MDBCG3fNHZJ/story.html |title=Catching up with Bruce Hurst, the Series MVP who wasn't |first=Dan |last=Shaughnessy |website=[[The Boston Globe]] |url-access=limited |date=December 1, 2015 |accessdate=November 2, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.barstoolsports.com/blog/3390509/on-this-date-in-sports-october-25-1986-game-6 |title=On This Date in Sports October 25, 1986: Game 6 |author=Frank The Tank |website=barstoolsports.com |date=October 25, 2021 |accessdate=November 2, 2024}}</ref> before the [[New York Mets]] staged a comeback and went on to win in seven games, with [[Ray Knight]] being named the MVP.
*1989 winner [[Dave Stewart (baseball)|Dave Stewart]] was the first pitcher to win two games each in a [[1989 American League Championship Series|League Championship Series]] and a World Series in the same postseason.
*1996 winner [[John Wetteland]] set a World Series record with four [[Save (baseball)|save]]s.<ref name="pwsr">{{cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/postseason/WS_pitching.shtml|title=All-time and Single-Season WS Pitching Leaders|publisher=Sports Reference, LLC|work=[[Baseball-Reference]]|access-date=October 3, 2009}}</ref>
*The 2001 co-MVPs, [[Randy Johnson]] and [[Curt Schilling]], combined for all four of Arizona's wins in the Series.<ref name="WS2001"/>
*[[Stephen Strasburg]], the 2019 winner, is the only first overall selection in a [[Major League Baseball draft]] to win the award.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.thescore.com/mlb/news/1806217 | title=Strasburg named World Series MVP | date=October 31, 2019 }}</ref>

===Position players===
*[[Bobby Richardson]], winner of the 1960 award, had 12 [[Run batted in|runs batted in]], a World Series record.<ref name="bwsr"/>
*1977 winner [[Reggie Jackson]] hit three home runs in the Series' deciding game, taking the nickname "Mr. October", as October is the primary month of the MLB postseason.<ref>{{cite news|last=Boeck|first=Scott|title=Reggie "Mr. October" Jackson thanks the Dodgers for his nickname|url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/dailypitch/post/2010/06/reggie-mr-october-jackson-thanks-the-dodgers-for-his-nickname/1|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=June 25, 2010|access-date=September 24, 2014}}</ref> Jackson had a total of five home runs in the series, a World Series record.<ref name="bwsr">{{cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/postseason/WS_batting.shtml|title=All-time and Single-Season WS Batting Leaders|publisher=Sports Reference, LLC|work=[[Baseball-Reference]]| access-date=October 3, 2009}}</ref>
*[[Willie Stargell]] won the 1979 award at the age of 39, and remains the oldest player to be named World Series MVP.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bloom|first=Barry M.|title=World Series MVP rewarding to Lowell|url=http://mlb.mlb.com/news/article.jsp?ymd=20071029&content_id=2286217&vkey=ps2007news&fext=.jsp&c_id=mlb|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|website=[[MLB.com]]|date=October 29, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071030000602/http://mlb.mlb.com/news/article.jsp?ymd=20071029&content_id=2286217&vkey=ps2007news&fext=.jsp&c_id=mlb|archive-date=2007-10-30|access-date=October 29, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[Barry Bonds]] was voted the [[2002 World Series]] MVP the day before the [[Los Angeles Angels|Anaheim Angels]] staged a comeback in Game 6 and won in seven games, resulting in [[Troy Glaus]] being named the MVP.
*[[Hideki Matsui]], the 2009 winner, batted in six runs in the sixth game of the [[2009 World Series]], tying Richardson's record for most runs batted in for a single World Series game. Matsui became the first Japanese-born player to win the award and the first player to win it as a full-time designated hitter.<ref>{{cite news|agency=[[Associated Press]]|title=Matsui Becomes 1st Japanese-Born World Series MVP|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=November 5, 2009|url=https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2009/11/05/sports/AP-BBO-World-Series-MVP.html|access-date=November 7, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mlb.mlb.com/news/article.jsp?ymd=20091104&content_id=7620234&vkey=news_mlb&fext=.jsp&c_id=mlb|title=Statsui: MVP delivers jaw-dropping numbers|publisher=[[Major League Baseball]]|access-date=November 4, 2009}}</ref> He is also the only player named both a World Series MVP and a [[Japan Series Most Valuable Player Award|Japan Series MVP]].<ref name="Japan Series MVP">{{cite web|url=http://search.japantimes.co.jp/cgi-bin/sb20100121a1.html|title=Matsui backs idea of global World Series|date=January 21, 2010|access-date=May 8, 2010|work=[[The Japan Times]]|last=Armstrong|first=Jim}}</ref>

===Other awards===
[[File:Willie Stargell - Pittsburgh Pirates - 1966.jpg|thumb|right|150px|[[Willie Stargell]] was named MLB MVP, LCS MVP, and World Series MVP in 1979.]]

Six pitchers have won the [[Cy Young Award]] and the World Series MVP in the same season: [[Bob Turley]] (1958), [[Whitey Ford]] (1961), Koufax (1963, 1965), [[Bret Saberhagen]] (1985), [[Orel Hershiser]] (1988), and Johnson (2001). The Cy Young Award was initiated in 1956, as one award for all of MLB; it has been awarded in both leagues since 1967.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.baseball-almanac.com/awards/aw_cyy.shtml |title=Cy Young Award |website=[[Baseball Almanac]] |accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref>

Nine players have been named both a [[League Championship Series Most Valuable Player Award|League Championship Series MVP]] and the World Series MVP in the same postseason: [[Willie Stargell]] (1979), [[Darrell Porter]] (1982), [[Orel Hershiser]] (1988), [[Liván Hernández]] (1997), [[Cole Hamels]] (2008), [[David Freese]] (2011), [[Madison Bumgarner]] (2014), [[Corey Seager]] (2020), and [[Jeremy Peña]] (2022). The LCS MVP was first awarded in 1977 for the [[National League (baseball)|National League]] and in 1980 for the [[American League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.baseball-almanac.com/awards/aw_mvpl.shtml |title=League Championship Most Valuable Player Award |website=[[Baseball Almanac]] |accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref>

To date, only one World Series MVP has also won the [[Major League Baseball All-Star Game Most Valuable Player Award]] in the same season: [[Derek Jeter]] in 2000. An All-Star Game MVP has been named since 1962.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.baseball-almanac.com/awards/aw_mvpa.shtml |title=MLB All-Star Game Most Valuable Player Award |website=[[Baseball Almanac]] |accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref>

Five players have received both a [[Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award]] and the World Series MVP Award in the same season: [[Sandy Koufax]] (1963), [[Frank Robinson]] (1966), [[Reggie Jackson]] (1973), [[Willie Stargell]] (1979), and [[Mike Schmidt]] (1980). The MLB MVP has been awarded to a player in each league since 1931.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.baseball-almanac.com/awards/aw_mvp.shtml |title=Most Valuable Player Award |website=[[Baseball Almanac]] |accessdate=November 1, 2024}}</ref>

Three players have won a World Series MVP plus two of the above awards in the same season:
*[[Sandy Koufax]] – MLB MVP, Cy Young, and World Series MVP in {{mlby|1963}}
*[[Willie Stargell]] – MLB MVP, LCS MVP, and World Series MVP in {{mlby|1979}}
*[[Orel Hershiser]] – Cy Young, LCS MVP, and World Series MVP in {{mlby|1988}}
